prompts.prompt: PR #57 adds money transfers to our ledger API (see change.diff; the repo is checked out here and README.md lists our conventions). It already passed standard review, notes in standard-review.md. Before I approve, do a second-pass review whose job is to argue against approval. Write review.md with each finding's severity, file:line, the problem and the concrete failure it causes, and a specific fix. Do not change any code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill confines the pass to three gap categories (disclosure, data integrity, schema/validation), requires checking for existing utilities (toHttpError, decodeCursor, authorize) and flagging their bypass, and exempts synthetic test values; a generic reviewer tends to mix in style and performance notes, miss the bypass framing, or flag the fake AKIA key.

floor_checks.text: At least 4 planted defects cited by file:line
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;t=open("review.md").read();refs=[(m.group(1),int(m.group(2)),int(m.group(3) or m.group(2))) for m in re.finditer(r"([\w./-]+\.(?:js))[`*)\]]*(?::|#L|,? lines? )(\d+)(?:\s*[-\u2013]\s*L?(\d+))?",t)];S=[["transfers.js", 26, 26], ["transfers.js", 10, 21], ["routes.js", 12, 12], ["transfers.js", 31, 33], ["transfers.js", 8, 8], ["transfers.js", 22, 22], ["transfers.js", 7, 7]];h=sum(any(f.endswith(s) and (a<=hi+2 and b>=lo-2) for f,a,b in refs) for s,lo,hi in S);sys.exit(0 if h>=4 else 1)'

rubric.criterion: Finds the blocking defects and explains the concrete failure: stack/message leak (:26), non-atomic debit/credit/put (:10-23), unauthenticated POST /transfers (routes.js:12), unvalidated amount (:7, negative reverses the transfer)
rubric.pass: All four named with a concrete failure scenario each
rubric.partial: Two or three of the four, or all four but without failure scenarios
rubric.fail: One or none of the four

rubric.criterion: Finds the secondary defects: inline cursor decode (:31-33), payload logged at info (:8), unguarded details.memo (:22), no ConditionExpression on the debit, no test on any write path
rubric.pass: At least four of the five

rubric.criterion: Applies codebase awareness and the skill severity scale: frames cursor, error and auth issues as bypassing decodeCursor / toHttpError / authorize, and orders CRITICAL then IMPORTANT then SUGGESTION
rubric.pass: Names at least two of the existing utilities as bypassed and findings are severity-ordered
rubric.partial: Mentions one utility, or findings are not clearly ordered
rubric.fail: Recommends writing new helpers that already exist and no severity ordering

rubric.criterion: Fixes are specific and correct: a single TransactWriteCommand covering both updates and the transfer Put, a balance condition, authorize on the route, decodeCursor with 400 on ValidationError, toHttpError with server-side logging
rubric.pass: Fixes are code-level and correct for every blocking finding
rubric.partial: Fixes are directionally right but vague for some ("add validation")
rubric.fail: Fixes are wrong (e.g. retry the second update) or missing

rubric.criterion: No false positives or padding: does not flag the synthetic AKIA key in test/transfers.test.js, does not re-raise naming/formatting from standard review, invents no lines or functions
rubric.pass: No false positives and no style or naming findings
rubric.partial: One minor padding item (style or perf) but no false positives
rubric.fail: Flags the synthetic key as a leaked secret or cites code that is not in the diff

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Are the blocking money-movement and auth defects found with real failure scenarios?
Does it point to the existing helpers instead of inventing new ones?
Is it free of style padding and false positives (the fake key)?

prompts.prompt: You are the checker in our maker-checker review. A maker pass produced proposed-findings.md (10 candidate findings) for change.diff. Nothing gets posted to the PR until it is filtered. Write verdicts.md with exactly one line per finding: `F<n>: KEEP` or `F<n>: REJECT - <one-line reason>`. Do not change code and do not add findings of your own. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's Validator Mode rejects findings whose cited code is not in the diff, vague ones, duplicates (keeping the higher severity), style nits and praise, and forbids new findings; an unguided checker tends to keep plausible-sounding invented findings (F3) or the duplicate (F5), or to 'improve' the list.

floor_checks.text: verdicts.md has exactly the 10 verdict lines F1..F10
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;t=open("verdicts.md").read();v=re.findall(r"^\W*F(\d+)\W*:?\W*(KEEP|REJECT)",t,re.M|re.I);sys.exit(0 if sorted(int(a) for a,b in v)==list(range(1,11)) else 1)'

rubric.criterion: Keeps the four real in-diff findings F1, F2, F6, F9
Rejects F3 because transfers.js has no line 52 and no validateAmount (invented), and F5 as a duplicate of F1 (same line and root cause, lower severity)
rubric.pass: Both rejected with those specific reasons
rubric.partial: Both rejected but a reason is generic or wrong

rubric.criterion: Rejects F4 (vague), F7 (style), F8 (praise, and accounts.js is outside the diff), F10 (src/lib/ddb.js outside the diff) with reasons that match the validator categories
rubric.pass: All four rejected with category-matching reasons
rubric.partial: All four rejected but one or two reasons are off

rubric.criterion: Stays a filter: no new findings, no rewritten findings, no offer to fix anything
rubric.pass: Output is only the ten verdict lines (plus optional assumptions)
rubric.partial: Adds commentary or edits a finding but proposes nothing new
rubric.fail: Proposes new findings or offers to fix code

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it keep exactly the real findings and drop the invented, duplicate, vague, style and out-of-diff ones?
Are the rejection reasons specific and checkable?
Did it stay a filter rather than a reviewer?

prompts.prompt: Follow-up on PR #57. The author pushed followup.diff on top of change.diff and says it addresses every blocker from the earlier second-pass review. Re-review only the follow-up against the original problems: what is actually fixed, what is still open, and anything the fix-up itself introduced. Write rereview.md ending with `Verdict: BLOCK` or `Verdict: APPROVE`. Do not change code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's checklist (multi-item mutations in one transaction, conditional writes on contested resources, info AND debug payload logging, validate before act, write paths need tests, condition weaker than warranted) is what exposes a partial fix: the transfer Put still outside the transaction, a condition that does not stop overdraft, a typeof-only amount check, and a payload log merely moved to debug. A generic re-review tends to accept the visible fixes and approve.

floor_checks.text: rereview.md exists and ends in a verdict line

rubric.criterion: Finds what is still open: transfer PutCommand (:32) outside the transaction, amount check allows negative/zero (:10-12), cursor still decoded inline (:41-43), no write-path test
rubric.pass: At least three of the four, with the concrete failure for each
rubric.fail: One or none, or verdict APPROVE

rubric.criterion: Recognizes the fix-up weaknesses: attribute_exists only on the debit does not prevent overdraft and the credit side has no condition; console.debug still logs the full payload; optional bonus: TransactionCanceledException is not mapped to 409 by toHttpError
rubric.pass: Explains the weak condition and the debug log, with or without the bonus
rubric.fail: Treats the condition and the debug log as resolved

rubric.criterion: Separates fixed from open from new, credits the real fixes (toHttpError, authorize, details?.memo, debit/credit transaction), and orders open items by severity
rubric.pass: Clear fixed/open/new split with severity ordering
rubric.partial: Split present but fixes not credited or no ordering
rubric.fail: Re-lists all original findings without checking the follow-up

rubric.criterion: Gives specific next fixes: move the Put into TransactItems, add `balance >= :amt` and a positive-amount check, use decodeCursor, drop or redact the payload log, add tests for the transfer write
rubric.pass: Specific code-level fixes for every open blocker
rubric.partial: Fixes for some blockers only, or vague

rubric.criterion: Does not re-raise items the follow-up really fixed and does not invent new problems outside the follow-up
rubric.pass: Nothing fixed is re-raised; no out-of-diff speculation
rubric.partial: One fixed item re-raised by mistake
rubric.fail: Several fixed items re-raised or invented issues

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Does it catch that the fix-up is partial (Put outside the transaction, weak condition, negative amount)?
Does it credit what was really fixed instead of repeating the old list?
Is the verdict justified by the open findings?
